finding: Saudi Arabia inspects accompanied plant products for personal consumption even when they are exempt from a phytosanitary certificate. The passenger allowances include up to 10 kg of fruit and vegetables excluding potatoes, and up to 30 kg of dates. Propagation seedlings must have a phytosanitary certificate, use a soil substitute and be of a permitted type. Permitted seeds must be packaged and sealed at origin, up to five packets of no more than 5 g each.
jurisdiction_scope: National inbound accompanied baggage; agricultural and veterinary quarantine guide, Chapter 5, Article 18. Decision 25083389 effective upon publication on 14 November 2025.
authority: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (official Umm Al-Qura gazette, issue 5122, via ILO NATLEX)
open_questions: Check current item and origin restrictions with the ministry, particularly for potatoes, animals, meat, dairy, soil and outdoor gear, which are outside this finding's coverage. Article 18 also lists separate caps of 7 trees/seedlings/shrubs, 20 cut flowers, 5 ornamental plants and 5 kg of flower bulbs or tubers.

finding: Visitors can apply to the Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture for entry permits for cats and dogs through the National Platform. Request clearance before traveling and check current breed eligibility, veterinary documentation and entry arrangements.
jurisdiction_scope: National visitor pet entry; National Platform expressly includes visitors, cats and dogs.
authority: Saudi National Platform / Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture
open_questions: Pet-import and return procedures, breed and carrier conditions and timing vary by itinerary. The ministry's separate veterinary quarantine guide lists cat vaccination and identification documents.

finding: Saudi wildlife regulations list importing, exporting, re-exporting or transiting with covered wildlife specimens, products or derivatives without a licence as violations. Confirm the species and licences before traveling with wildlife-derived souvenirs.
jurisdiction_scope: National border; Executive Regulation on the Protection of Wildlife, Wildlife Products and Derivatives, table 1, for specimens on convention and designated national lists.
authority: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture / National Center for Wildlife (Umm Al-Qura official gazette)
open_questions: Confirm species, both countries' requirements, relevant CITES appendix, and any personal-effects exception with the management authorities before travel.

finding: Saudi customs lists books and publications that violate Ministry of Media regulations among travelers' prohibited goods. Confirm questionable titles or materials with Saudi customs before packing them.
jurisdiction_scope: National passenger customs ports; books and publications covered by media regulations.
authority: Saudi Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority
open_questions: The cited list does not identify every title, religious item or permitted quantity.

finding: Saudi customs exempts up to 200 regular cigarettes from customs duties and taxes. For quantities above 200 and below 2,400, its guidance requires Saudi Food and Drug Authority approval and applies duties and taxes to the whole quantity. Check separate customs rules for vapes and refills.
jurisdiction_scope: National inbound accompanied regular cigarettes; traveler guidance updated 26 August 2026.
authority: Saudi Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority
open_questions: Exactly 2,400 cigarettes is not covered by the examples. Confirm vaping devices, refill liquids and other products under the applicable rules.

finding: Article 42 of the Traffic Law limits recognized foreign or international driving licence validity to one year after entry or the licence expiry date, whichever comes first. Verify recognition and any rental or insurer requirements before driving.
jurisdiction_scope: National driving documentation; Articles 37 and 42, Traffic Law.
authority: Saudi National Center for Archives and Records / Traffic Law
open_questions: Check the issuing country and format, any translation or international permit requirement, and rental terms.

finding: If you brought an antiquity or heritage item into Saudi Arabia, Article 40 requires a customs declaration and registration within three weeks after entry. Approval from the heritage authority is needed to take that item back out.
jurisdiction_scope: National re-export of previously imported antiquities or heritage items; Law of Antiquities, Museums and Urban Heritage, Article 40.
authority: Saudi Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers
open_questions: Confirm the current Heritage Commission application and customs release process for the item.

finding: Leave underwater archaeological sites, shipwrecks and movable antiquities where they are and report discoveries promptly to the heritage authority or nearest government authority. The law requires accidentally recovered antiquities to be reported and handed over within one week.
jurisdiction_scope: National waters under Saudi sovereignty or jurisdiction; Law of Antiquities, Museums and Urban Heritage, Article 27.
authority: Saudi Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers
open_questions: Check local dive-site access rules and current reporting channels.

finding: Saudi drug law allows a patient to possess controlled narcotic or psychotropic medicine prescribed by a licensed physician under the law and prohibits transferring it to others. Keep the approval and prescription documentation for any controlled medicine cleared by SFDA for personal travel.
jurisdiction_scope: National in-country personal possession; Narcotics and Psychotropics Control Law, Article 35.
authority: Saudi Food and Drug Authority
open_questions: Confirm personal-import clearance separately and check the active ingredient with SFDA.

finding: Carry a valid driving licence while driving in Saudi Arabia. Traffic Law Article 33 permits law enforcement to inspect it.
jurisdiction_scope: National on-road conduct; Traffic Law, Articles 32 and 33.
authority: Saudi National Center for Archives and Records / Traffic Law
open_questions: Check separate licence recognition, insurance, vehicle documentation and local road rules.

finding: Saudi protected-area regulations list leaving, throwing away, burying or burning waste in a protected area without National Center for Wildlife authorization as a violation. Follow the reserve's waste instructions and take your waste out when facilities are unavailable.
jurisdiction_scope: Saudi protected areas governed by this regulation; violations table, item 15.
authority: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture / National Center for Wildlife (Umm Al-Qura official gazette)
open_questions: Check local operating rules and disposal arrangements for the reserve.

finding: Do not collect products or derivatives of threatened or prohibited wildlife in Saudi protected areas. Collecting other covered wildlife specimens, products or derivatives in these areas requires a licence.
jurisdiction_scope: Saudi protected areas governed by this regulation; violations table, items 7 and 8.
authority: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture / National Center for Wildlife (Umm Al-Qura official gazette)
open_questions: Check exact species and site rules, especially for shells or coral. Sand and ordinary rocks are not evaluated by this finding.

finding: In protected areas designated by the National Center for Wildlife, use designated vehicle tracks and obtain a licence before camping. The Saudi protected-area regulation lists breaches as violations.
jurisdiction_scope: National Center for Wildlife designated protected areas; violations table, items 13 and 14.
authority: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture / National Center for Wildlife (Umm Al-Qura official gazette)
open_questions: Check area-specific access, driving, camping and operator rules.

finding: Saudi Ministry of Tourism guidance requires guests to present identification to tourist accommodation for verification and recordkeeping. Visitors should bring their passport to check-in.
jurisdiction_scope: National tourist accommodation establishments; accepted identification includes passport, national ID or residence permit.
authority: Saudi Ministry of Tourism
open_questions: For alternative identification or an exception, confirm with the establishment and competent authority. Separate police registration was not established.

finding: Saudi tourist eVisa terms state that non-Muslims may not enter the Holy Mosque or its premises in Makkah or the Prophet's Mosque or its premises in Madinah.
jurisdiction_scope: Saudi tourist eVisa terms, §12; specified holy sites and premises.
authority: Saudi official tourist eVisa portal
open_questions: Confirm the precise access boundaries and separate seasonal Hajj restrictions before travel.

finding: Saudi Ministry of Tourism guidance says licensed tourist accommodation should offer Visa or Mastercard credit-card payment or other options approved in the Kingdom. Confirm the property's accepted payment methods and booking conditions before you pay.
jurisdiction_scope: National tourist accommodation; payment guidance applies to hospitality services.
authority: Saudi Ministry of Tourism
open_questions: General merchant or cash-acceptance rules are outside this finding.

finding: Quarantine Act section 15 requires travellers to answer relevant screening or quarantine officer questions, provide reasonably required information or records in their possession, and comply with reasonable disease-control measures ordered by those officers. Disclose reasonable suspicion of a disease listed in the Act, vector infestation, or qualifying recent close proximity.
jurisdiction_scope: Canada federal quarantine screening, including at ports of entry. The disclosure duty applies to the statutory circumstances.
authority: Department of Justice Canada, Quarantine Act section 15
open_questions: Check the current statutory schedule and Public Health Agency of Canada instructions for a specific exposure or itinerary. Routine vaccination and immigration medical examinations are separate topics.

finding: Under Canada's temporary Ebola border order, eligible entrants who were in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda or South Sudan in the 21 days before entry must disclose that travel and undergo a health assessment. Entrants assessed as asymptomatic generally must present a suitable plan and quarantine for 21 days starting on their entry day. Symptomatic entrants are subject to medical examination and isolation. A separate provision generally bars foreign nationals who were in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the preceding 21 days, with exceptions in section 4.
jurisdiction_scope: Canada federal entry, route and status conditions under Order P.C. 2026-0873. The order is scheduled to end November 27, 2026 at 23:59:59 Eastern Standard Time, with continuing obligations under section 16(2) through December 17 for covered entrants arriving November 8–27.
authority: Governor in Council, Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to Ebola Disease in Canada Order, 2026, No. 3
open_questions: Time-sensitive. Recheck for a superseding order or changed country assessment before display. Apply sections 2–4 and 10 for distinct airside-transit, entry-prohibition and quarantine exceptions. Section 10 quarantine exemptions still require symptom monitoring. Follow section 16's EST deadline where public summaries say EDT. Check separate IRCC immigration-document measures if applicable.

finding: Immigration medical examinations generally are not required for visits of six months or less, with exceptions for certain jobs. For stays over six months, an examination can be required based on documented residence or travel history in designated places, protected public-health occupations, or a parent and grandparent super visa.
jurisdiction_scope: Canada immigration applications for temporary residents including visitors, students and workers.
authority: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
open_questions: Check duration, occupation, visa class, the current designated country list and qualifying in-Canada exemptions. This is an immigration application rule.

finding: Canada's Criminal Code makes wearing a military uniform without lawful authority an offence. The provision also covers a uniform likely to be mistaken for one and specifies related restrictions on wearing certain military decorations or imitations.
jurisdiction_scope: Canada federal law, in-country wearing of military uniforms and specified decorations without lawful authority.
authority: Department of Justice Canada, Criminal Code section 419
open_questions: Apply the statutory test to the attire and occasion. This source does not establish border import controls or classify everyday camouflage-pattern clothing.

finding: Canada generally prohibits possession of substances listed in Schedules I to III of the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act unless authorized by regulations.
jurisdiction_scope: Canada federal possession law, specified controlled substances in country.
authority: Department of Justice Canada, Controlled Drugs and Substances Act section 4
open_questions: Confirm the exact substance, current schedule, regulatory authorization and applicable exemptions. International carriage is tracked separately under MEDICINE.

finding: Ontario hotels must keep a guest register that includes one guest's name, residence details and primary phone number, plus details of guest vehicles parked on the premises. Covered online platforms instead record the person making a short-term reservation and their billing address and phone number, plus vehicle details if known at reservation.
jurisdiction_scope: Ontario only. Accommodation-provider and covered online-platform recordkeeping, effective January 1, 2026.
authority: Ontario e-Laws, O. Reg. 292/25 and Accommodation Sector Registration of Guests Act, 2021
open_questions: Check the accommodation type and provider process. Other provinces and territories require separate review. Source for hotel name and residence fields: https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/21a21a

finding: British Columbia emergency powers allow authorities to limit or prohibit travel to or from a specified area and require evacuation. Check active orders before travelling in affected areas and follow the issuing authority's directions.
jurisdiction_scope: British Columbia only; restrictions depend on a currently applicable order or emergency instrument, its geography, duration and exceptions.
authority: British Columbia Laws, Emergency and Disaster Management Act sections 77, 78 and 107
open_questions: Check the issuing local authority and the active notices at https://www.emergencyinfobc.gov.bc.ca/ for the route and dates.

finding: Canadian notes and coins are legal tender, but the Bank of Canada says merchants may choose how to take payment. Confirm accepted methods before relying on cash alone.
jurisdiction_scope: Canada, ordinary retail payment methods accepted by merchants.
authority: Bank of Canada
open_questions: Check the individual merchant's payment policy. Transactions under specific contracts or regulatory frameworks are outside this finding.

finding: Bring a reusable shopping bag in Penang. The state campaign guidelines call for a phased rollout from 1 September 2025 under which eight types of locally registered retail premises stop supplying single-use plastic carrier bags daily. Product, food and drink wrappers are outside the campaign definition.
jurisdiction_scope: Penang retail premises covered by local licensing guidance.
authority: Penang state campaign guidelines published by Seberang Perai City Council
open_questions: Check premise category and phase with the local council. This is a retail policy and its scope does not establish a baggage import restriction.

finding: Royal Malaysian Customs excludes cigarettes, tobacco products, electronic cigarettes and their liquid or gel preparations from the general passenger duty-free allowance for both air and non-air arrivals. Its passenger guide separately lists a combined one-litre duty and tax exemption for wine, spirits, beer or malt liquor, subject to the exemption conditions. Ask Customs about duty and applicable product rules before carrying these items.
jurisdiction_scope: Passenger imports into Malaysia by air and non-air routes, customs duty and tax treatment.
authority: Royal Malaysian Customs Department
open_questions: Confirm item-specific admissibility and current exemption conditions, including any rules for special customs areas. No vape import-ban conclusion follows from the duty exclusion.

finding: The First Schedule of Malaysia’s 2023 Customs (Prohibition of Imports) Order includes cloth and animal skin printed with Quranic verses among goods prohibited from import, regardless of origin. Check with Royal Malaysian Customs before packing garments or textiles that fall under that description.
jurisdiction_scope: Malaysia customs imports of cloth or animal skin bearing printed or reproduced Quranic verses, First Schedule item 3.
authority: Malaysia federal gazette, published by Royal Malaysian Customs Department
open_questions: Confirm treatment of unusual items and check subsequent amendments. Camouflage and uniform rules remain unverified in this finding.

finding: The First Schedule of Malaysia’s 2023 Customs (Prohibition of Imports) Order prohibits import of material classified as indecent or obscene, including covered books, photographs, films and other media. If unsure how an item is classified, check with Royal Malaysian Customs before carrying it.
jurisdiction_scope: Malaysia customs imports from all origins under First Schedule item 5.
authority: Malaysia federal gazette, published by Royal Malaysian Customs Department
open_questions: Check current amendments and item classification. General religious publications and digital transmission were not assessed.

finding: At protected heritage sites in Malaysia, leave monuments and site materials in place. National Heritage Act section 112 requires the Commissioner’s written approval to mark, disturb, modify or remove a monument in a heritage site or to excavate in a heritage site or conservation area.
jurisdiction_scope: Statutory heritage sites, monuments and conservation areas within the scope of Malaysia’s National Heritage Act 2005.
authority: Department of National Heritage, Malaysia
open_questions: Check site designation and additional local or site-specific conditions with the operator.

finding: Check the rules of the Malaysian state or Federal Territory before planning religious outreach to Muslims. Federal Constitution Article 11(4) allows state law, and federal law in Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya, to control or restrict propagation of religious doctrines to people professing Islam.
jurisdiction_scope: Constitutional authority for jurisdiction-specific restrictions on religious propagation in Malaysia.
authority: Federal Constitution, published by Malaysia’s Judicial Appointments Commission
open_questions: Check current implementing law where the outreach will take place. This entry covers legal authority only and leaves local offences and other speech restrictions unverified.

finding: Have your passport details available at paid accommodation check-in. Section 3 of the Registration of Guests Act 1965 requires covered operators to record qualifying guests aged 12 or over and collect passport particulars when the guest has no identity card. Covered guests must furnish the required details and sign the register.
jurisdiction_scope: Malaysia paid lodging premises and guests covered by Act 381 section 3; children under 12 and servants of the keeper are excluded from the cited requirement.
authority: Malaysia federal statute (Act 381), reproduced by China’s Ministry of Commerce policy portal
open_questions: Confirm current text or amendments on Malaysia’s federal legislation portal and any applicable local lodging procedures before release.

finding: Ask local police and your licensed operator about current maritime movement controls before booking a boat transfer, night dive or other water activity off eastern Sabah. Australian government travel advice reports overnight water-travel restrictions in parts of eastern Sabah and permit requirements on certain daytime routes. Local orders can change.
jurisdiction_scope: Selected eastern Sabah coastal waters and maritime activities; Australian consular advisory.
authority: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Smartraveller)
open_questions: Obtain the currently applicable Malaysian police order, expiry, exact districts, operating hours and permit procedure before publishing any specific curfew details.

finding: If you plan to transmit on amateur radio in Malaysia, check authorization with MCMC before operating. Where a reciprocal arrangement exists, eligible foreign operators may apply for a reciprocal assignment. Other cases are handled through special arrangements on application.
jurisdiction_scope: Operation of amateur radio stations in Malaysia by visiting foreign amateur radio operators.
authority: Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, Amateur Radio Service Guidelines, sections 41–44
open_questions: Confirm home-country reciprocity, equipment, band and call-sign conditions. Satellite phones and routine mobile devices were not assessed.

finding: Bank Negara Malaysia’s Foreign Exchange Policy Notice 4 allows a nonresident to make or receive ringgit payments in Malaysia for local expenses and qualifying purchases of goods or services. Confirm the merchant’s accepted payment method before relying on a particular card or digital wallet.
jurisdiction_scope: Domestic payments in ringgit by nonresidents in Malaysia, Notice 4 Part B paragraph 2.
authority: Bank Negara Malaysia
open_questions: Merchant acceptance, account due diligence and border currency declaration rules are separate.

finding: Before taking an antique or possible heritage item out of Peninsular Malaysia or Labuan, ask the Department of National Heritage whether it is a statutory heritage item. Section 83 of the National Heritage Act requires an export licence for covered heritage items. If you depart from Sabah or Sarawak, check with the applicable museum authority for the local licence rules.
jurisdiction_scope: Export licensing for Malaysia statutory heritage items; core section 83 alert scoped to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan.
authority: Department of National Heritage, Malaysia
open_questions: Confirm classification with the competent authority and review Customs Order P.U. (A) 122/2023 item 30 and its current amendments; Sabah and Sarawak have distinct issuing authorities.

finding: Do not enter or drive into a designated military restricted area without authorization. For qualifying reasons the competent military office may authorize access and impose conditions.
jurisdiction_scope: Designated Austrian military restricted areas under the Restricted Areas Act; ordinary public areas outside the designation are outside this rule.
authority: Austrian federal legal information system, Sperrgebietsgesetz 2002 §§ 1–3
open_questions: Check the current designation and authorized access with the competent military office.

finding: Austria generally prohibits photographing or filming designated military restricted areas and military installations within them. Obtain consent from the competent military office before recording a restricted area if you need an exception.
jurisdiction_scope: Designated Austrian military restricted areas and installations in them, with statutory exceptions and authorization provisions.
authority: Austrian federal legal information system, Sperrgebietsgesetz 2002 §4
open_questions: Observe the designation and any permission conditions.

finding: Avoid conduct that disturbs public order and is liable to cause justified offense. It may be an administrative offense unless legally justified, including by exercise of a constitutional right.
jurisdiction_scope: Federal public-order provision; the circumstances and lawful justification matter.
authority: Austrian federal legal information system, Sicherheitspolizeigesetz §81

finding: Austrian criminal law covers certain public ridicule or denigration of a religion’s objects of veneration, doctrines, lawful customs or institutions when the circumstances are liable to cause justified offense.
jurisdiction_scope: Federal criminal law; applies to covered churches and religious societies established in Austria and requires the statutory public and contextual elements.
authority: Austrian federal legal information system, Criminal Code §188

finding: Unauthorized possession of scheduled narcotic drugs is an offense in Austria. Check the specific substance and keep the documents required for any prescribed controlled medicine you carry during the visit.
jurisdiction_scope: In-country possession of substances covered by the Addictive Substances Act §27(1)(1); lawful medical use is governed separately.
authority: Austrian federal legal information system, Suchtmittelgesetz §27
open_questions: Check the exact medicine and applicable authorization with the Austrian health authority; separate entry guidance is recorded under MEDICINE.

finding: In Vienna, children under 14 may generally be in publicly accessible places and attend public events from 05:00 to 23:00. Ages 14–15 generally have until 01:00. Outside those hours an eligible accompanying person or a justified reason such as the trip home can provide an exception.
jurisdiction_scope: Vienna youth-protection rules for publicly accessible places and public events; traveler age and accompaniment matter. Other Austrian provinces have their own rules.
authority: Vienna Youth Protection Act §8, Austrian federal legal information system
open_questions: Check event-specific age or closing restrictions and §3 for the definition of eligible accompanying person.

finding: Register in advance on BerlengasPass before visiting the land area of Berlenga Island and pay any applicable access fee. Check registration and availability before booking your boat.
jurisdiction_scope: Land access to Berlenga Island, Berlengas Nature Reserve, Peniche. Maritime access and activity permissions are separate.
authority: Diário da República, Portaria 30/2021; BerlengasPass operated by ICNF
open_questions: Check current fees, exemptions and date availability at https://berlengaspass.icnf.pt/faq. Fee order is updated annually.

finding: Before packing amateur transmitting equipment for use in Portugal, confirm that your credential is recognized and that your station can meet Portuguese operating conditions. The national law recognizes qualifying valid CEPT, ITU or reciprocal-country documents for operation under the applicable rules.
jurisdiction_scope: Amateur transmitting station operation in Portugal under Decree-Law 53/2009 as amended by Law 22/2026; this finding concerns preparation for lawful use.
authority: Portuguese Parliament, Law 22/2026, republished Decree-Law 53/2009 Article 8(3)
open_questions: Check current ANACOM implementing rules, call-sign and frequencies. Equipment import and unrelated radio services were not assessed.

finding: For naturism at a Portuguese beach, look for a locally authorized, marked naturist area. National law provides for municipal authorization of all or part of a beach and requires signs at access points.
jurisdiction_scope: Authorized Portuguese sea, river and lake naturist beaches under Law 53/2010, Articles 8–10.
authority: Diário da República, Law 53/2010
open_questions: Confirm the current authorized section with the municipality and on-site signage. This finding addresses the statutory designation and signs.

finding: Parques de Sintra limits general visitor images to private purposes where allowed by signs and staff. No images are allowed inside Pena Palace; indoor flash, drones and tripods are also restricted under the general visitor policy.
jurisdiction_scope: Heritage sites managed by Parques de Sintra. Published venue policy, including written permission for exceptional tripod use and a separate authorization procedure for public or commercial images.
authority: Parques de Sintra, Image Capture Regulations
open_questions: Check the exact site and permissions before filming; national drone rules apply separately.

finding: In Lisbon, covered vendors cannot sell alcohol for street consumption from 23:00 to 08:00 Sunday through Thursday, or midnight to 08:00 Friday, Saturday and holiday eves. Licensed terraces may serve seated customers during permitted hours.
jurisdiction_scope: Municipality of Lisbon, in force from 15 February 2026. The measure regulates vendor sales for outside consumption during specified hours.
authority: Lisbon City Council, citywide street-consumption alcohol sales schedule
open_questions: Check municipal guidance for venue and holiday scope.

finding: Portugal’s Criminal Code covers publicly insulting or mocking someone because of their religious beliefs or role when the conduct is liable to disturb public peace.
jurisdiction_scope: National Criminal Code Article 251(1). Both the religious basis and public-peace condition matter.
authority: Portuguese Criminal Code, Article 251(1), Diário da República

finding: Before taking amateur radio equipment to Austria for use, check your license class. Visitors aged 14 or over holding a qualifying foreign CEPT or CEPT Novice license may set up and operate a station for three months from entry. These licenses do not authorize onboard aircraft operation.
jurisdiction_scope: Amateur radio station operation in Austria under Amateurfunkverordnung §3, with eligibility, class and aircraft limitations.
authority: Austrian federal legal information system, Amateurfunkverordnung §3
open_questions: Check current operating class and limits with Fernmeldebehörde. Equipment import was not assessed.

finding: Before packing a walkie-talkie for Poland, check that it is a compliant PMR446 device if you plan to transmit without a radio permit. The regulator identifies technical conditions including maximum radiated power and a factory-integrated antenna.
jurisdiction_scope: Poland; intended operation of handheld radios while visiting.
authority: Office of Electronic Communications (UKE)
open_questions: Verify the model and applicable technical conditions with UKE. This addresses transmitting and leaves any customs or carriage requirements to their respective checks.

finding: Before bringing material into Poland for distribution, check whether it is covered by Criminal Code Article 256. The law prohibits specified acts including importing or transporting covered propaganda or hate-incitement material for distribution, with exceptions for artistic, educational, collecting and scientific activities.
jurisdiction_scope: Poland; conduct involving an intent to distribute specified material under Article 256(2).
authority: Polish Criminal Code, Article 256(1)–(3)
open_questions: Material, purpose and statutory exception are fact-dependent. This evidence does not establish a general restriction on personal books or religious texts.

finding: Check entry fees and buy a ticket before entering Poland's Tatra National Park unless eligible for an exemption. The park’s 2026 instructions list park-gate ticket points and statutory fee exemptions.
jurisdiction_scope: Tatra National Park on the Polish side only.
authority: Tatra National Park visitor ticket instructions for 2026
open_questions: Recheck entry fees, exemptions and which ticket point and trail are open for your date. Slovakia’s park has separate rules.

finding: When sightseeing in Wawel Cathedral, cover shoulders and back, silence your phone and keep quiet. The Cathedral prohibits sightseeing during religious services.
jurisdiction_scope: Wawel Cathedral, Kraków; venue conditions for sightseeing.
authority: Wawel Cathedral parish visitor regulations
open_questions: Check current visitor hours and conditions before arrival.

finding: Polish criminal law covers malicious disruption of specified public religious rites and acts that offend others’ religious feelings by publicly insulting a religious object or a place designated for public rites.
jurisdiction_scope: Poland; conduct defined in Criminal Code Articles 195–196.
authority: Polish Criminal Code, Articles 195–196
open_questions: Check current text and seek qualified advice for a particular event or proposed conduct.

finding: Unauthorized possession of narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances is a criminal offense in Poland. If a prescribed medicine is controlled, check the separate personal medical-use documentation requirements with Poland’s pharmaceutical inspectorate.
jurisdiction_scope: Poland; possession under the Act on Counteracting Drug Addiction.
authority: Polish Act on Counteracting Drug Addiction, Articles 62–62a
open_questions: Confirm the active ingredient against the current controlled list and consult the separate MEDICINE entry on documents.

finding: Stay outside the restricted portions of Poland's border zone with Belarus unless an exception or authorization applies. The existing order runs through 29 November 2026. The successor order takes effect on 30 November 2026 and imposes a 90-day prohibition in areas specified in its text. Check your itinerary with the Polish Border Guard.
jurisdiction_scope: Specified parts of the Poland–Belarus border zone only; time-limited security restriction.
authority: Polish Ministry of Interior and Administration, Journal of Laws 2026 item 1550, sections 1–2
open_questions: Earlier order through 29 November: https://www.gov.pl/web/mswia/przedluzenie-strefy-buforowej-na-granicy-polsko-bialoruskiej2. Check exact limits, statutory exceptions or permissions and any latest extensions before visiting.

finding: Before packing a two-way radio for the European Netherlands, check whether you can use it on the license-exempt PMR446 frequencies for handheld radios or whether your intended operation requires a permit.
jurisdiction_scope: European Netherlands; intended handheld radio operation.
authority: Dutch Authority for Digital Infrastructure (RDI)
open_questions: Confirm the specific radio and frequencies with RDI. Separate rules may govern customs, air carriage or other transmitters.

finding: If arriving in the Netherlands from outside the EU with an old book or document that qualifies as a cultural good, declare it to Dutch Customs. Dutch Customs lists old books and documents as examples and says that in some cases an import licence or importer declaration is required.
jurisdiction_scope: European Netherlands; travelers bringing qualifying cultural goods from outside the European Union.
authority: Dutch Customs
open_questions: Confirm the item's age, value, origin, classification and whether an import licence or declaration applies. This Dutch example gives traveler guidance for a subset of the existing EU cultural-goods rule.

finding: Plan a guided excursion if you want to enter the core of Oostvaardersplassen. The site manager restricts core access to excursions outside winter. Parts of some surrounding areas and trails also close in winter and sometimes into spring.
jurisdiction_scope: Oostvaardersplassen, Flevoland; conditions differ between the core and surrounding areas.
authority: Staatsbosbeheer, national public land manager
open_questions: Check the manager’s current closure notices and permitted routes or book an available excursion.

finding: Before posting trip photos or video of identifiable people publicly, check whether you have a lawful basis. The Dutch privacy regulator says purely personal or household use can cover keeping images private or sharing in a very limited circle. Consent is usually the basis for ordinary publication on social media.
jurisdiction_scope: European Netherlands; handling of images containing identifiable people.
authority: Dutch Data Protection Authority
open_questions: Check the basis for a particular publication, any journalism exception and any separate venue photography rules.

finding: Dutch criminal law prohibits intentionally insulting a group of people in public on the basis of religion or belief, including through speech, writing or images. The Public Prosecution Service treats the legal assessment as context-specific.
jurisdiction_scope: European Netherlands; public group insult under Dutch Criminal Code Article 137c.
authority: Dutch Public Prosecution Service
open_questions: Do not generalize the offense to criticism of a religion itself. See also https://www.om.nl/onderwerpen/d/discriminatie.

finding: Possessing illicit drugs is an offense in the Netherlands, including recreational cannabis. The Dutch government describes a limited non-prosecution policy for adults with small personal quantities of cannabis. Police can still seize it. Check controlled prescriptions under the separate medicine documentation guidance.
jurisdiction_scope: European Netherlands; in-country possession and prosecution policy.
authority: Government of the Netherlands
open_questions: Border transport and lawful prescribed medicines are separate checks. Municipal rules can also restrict public use.

finding: Amsterdam police can impose individual bans on remaining in designated nuisance areas. If an exclusion order is issued to you, follow its area and duration. Ask the city for temporary access if you have a qualifying need such as medical care or work.
jurisdiction_scope: Amsterdam only; individual stay-away notices in designated areas.
authority: City of Amsterdam
open_questions: Read the notice and consult https://www.amsterdam.nl/leefomgeving/toegang-vragen-gebiedsverbod/ if access is required.
